full_model_64tok: outputs byte-identical across 4L-capture/4L-replay/8L-replay; demand 905.8 MiB exact in all; reads 8471.4/8471.4/8472.9 MiB
decision_note: Deterministic capture/replay accepted as benchmark infrastructure; it removes route-dependent work variance. The 8-lane retrial inside it shows a cold-phase-only benefit: +12.4% first-32 with flat last-32, so eight lanes are a cold-start profile, not a sustained speedup.

Deterministic fixed-workload retrial attributes the earlier gain entirely to the cache-fill phase: warm-window speed is unchanged and the +3% sustained bar is not met. Rejected as a general speedup; --io-threads 8 stays available as a cold-start profile for short interactive bmoe-cli runs. The interactive server runs the separate expert-tier binary and is unaffected.

The 14-15 interactive observation is the distinct-prompt band; repeated-prompt peaks at 18.09. True cold start is a 1 tok/s cliff with silent 435 MiB process swap. This is the new practical baseline for Qwen3.8.

outputs: byte-identical A vs B on all four prompts
decision_note: Patches accepted as stability improvement: same speed (−0.55% inside spread), byte-identical output, 12.9 GiB less peak RSS via the loader fix, pinned staging active. Cold-swap parity on an empty page cache remains unverified.

reason: The cold run overlapped a parallel 16-thread build on the same CPU; --cpu-moe generation is CPU-bound, so the numbers were contaminated, not reproduced.

decision_note: Cold start is a ~12 tok/s phase, not a 1 tok/s cliff; the 435 MiB swap claim is unconfirmed and must not be cited. Warm figures (18.09 repeated / 13.5-15.4 distinct) are unaffected - no parallel load existed during them.

functional_gate: one live slot, 996 MiB exact allocation, coherent 16-token generation, zero process swap
decision_note: Exact layout sizing, allocation backoff, and runtime headroom make explicit autofit fail safe; performance activation is rejected by EXP-010.

decision_note: Live hot store regressed decode and failed deterministic output stability. Launcher default changed to EHS=0; autofit remains explicit experimental mode only.

decision_note: Cold decode pays substantial mmap-backed storage faults; warm decode is CPU-saturated with negligible physical I/O and low GPU utilization. Prefetch targets cold latency only; sustained speed requires CPU/GPU compute work.

correctness_gate: passed: identical SHA-256 in all 20 requests
decision_note: Per-MUL_MAT_ID POSIX_MADV_WILLNEED reduced cold reads and major faults but materially slowed both cold and warm generation. Runtime code removed; patch retained for analysis.

warm.correctness_gate: identical SHA-256 in all six measured requests

decision_note: Launcher default changed from 16 to 12 threads as an explicitly accepted resource-efficiency tradeoff: effectively identical single-stream speed with about 25% fewer occupied CPU cores. THREADS=16 remains available.

correctness_gate: identical SHA-256 across warmup, reference, and profiled requests
decision_note: Warm decode is split between quantized vector-dot arithmetic and OpenMP spin/wait overhead. Test a separate GGML_OPENMP=OFF build before changing quant kernels.
No positive signal justified a long A/B. Keep GGML_OPENMP=ON; do not claim the native pool retained an exact 39.96% wait share because the OFF arm was not perf-profiled.

workload: one cold 128-token MTP request under perf record -e major-faults:u; diagnostic, not a speed comparison
decision_note: Cold-start major faults are 99.83% inside model file mappings and 95.07% of all faults land in ffn_*_exps expert tensors (99.9% of in-mapping model faults excluding MTP head). Cold I/O is expert weights, which validates the P1 expert-residency direction. A simple madvise variant was already rejected in EXP-012, so the follow-up is early prefetch/async reading ahead of expert matmuls, not a flag change. Offline Perl sum bug fixed: the down/gate/up three-way total is 206114, not the down-only 99154 the first pass reported.

hypothesis: background re-read of heatmap top-S expert slices keeps the working set in page cache so later requests after eviction avoid disk faults
blocking_finding: real in-session eviction of expert pages destabilized the CUDA driver: 3 of 4 runs aborted in cudaGraphExecDestroy with libc heap corruption inside libcuda at ~token 215-218 of the first request; runs without real eviction complete normally
decision_note: No speed signal (kernel readahead already overlaps fault-fill with compute; consistent with EXP-012) and the eviction hook is unsafe. Warmer code removed from runtime and patch. P1 closed: no remaining prefetch/residency lever has expected positive value.
